"'''Beyond the Sea'''" is the third episode of the sixth series of the anthology series ''[[Black Mirror]]''. It was written by the series creator [[Charlie Brooker]] and directed by [[John Crowley (director)|John Crowley]]. Alongside the rest of the sixth series, it premiered on Netflix on 15 June 2023. Set in a [[Retrofuturism|retrofuturistic]] 1969, it follows two astronauts, Cliff ([[Aaron Paul]]) and David ([[Josh Hartnett]]), who inhabit replicas of their bodies on Earth. The astronauts grapple with an unfathomable tragedy that occurs on Earth.

Brooker conceived of the episode as a story about [[working from home]]. It was influenced by the [[Manson Family]] cult active in the 1960s. The title comes from [[Beyond the Sea (song)|an English version]] of "[[La Mer (song)|La Mer]]", a song prominent in the episode. Filming took place for three weeks in summer 2022 across multiple locations; namely [[Whitstable]], [[Rye, East Sussex|Rye]] and [[Dungeness]] in England. Filming also took place across both London and Spain. Aaron Paul, a fan of ''Black Mirror'', plays both Cliff and David inhabiting Cliff's replica. He had agreed to a cameo in the fourth series opener "[[USS Callister|USS ''Callister'']]" in 2017 under the condition that he could appear in the series again.

Critics identified the episode as character-driven: Cliff is more strict and uptight than David. The masculinity of each character is explored, as is Lana's experience of isolation. The acting was widely praised by reviewers, as was the episode's emotional, contemplative tone, although the plot and pacing garnered a mixed reaction. Overall, many critics considered it the best episode of the sixth series.

== Plot ==
In an [[alternate history]] 1969, Cliff Stanfield ([[Aaron Paul]]) and David Ross ([[Josh Hartnett]]) are astronauts two years into a six-year mission. They can transfer their consciousness to artificial copies of their bodies on Earth when not needed on the ship for routine checks and exercise.

As Cliff and his wife Lana ([[Kate Mara]]) recently moved to the countryside with their son Henry, Lana suggests a garden party to meet neighbours, but Cliff rejects the idea. David goes to the movies with his son, daughter, and wife Jessica ([[Auden Thornton]]) for his son's birthday. He dances to "[[La Mer (song)|La Mer]]" with Jessica and they share an intimate moment. David and Cliff are both interrupted by an alert, leading the two to return to their real bodies. On the station, Cliff repairs the solar coating of the station while David supervises. They then return to their replica bodies on Earth.

At night, David hears intruders and approaches with a baseball bat. The four intruders—led by Kappa ([[Rory Culkin]])—comprise a cult that oppose artificial humans. They tie David up; he watches as they kill his family and destroy his replica.

Restricted to the spaceship, David falls silent in grief and is at risk of [[suicide]], which greatly worries Cliff, as it takes two people to run the ship. At Lana's suggestion, Cliff lets David use his replica to walk through the forest. David, in Cliff's replica, breaks down in tears and Lana embraces him.

Back on the ship, Cliff is heartened by David's drawing of his house from memory and allows David to use his replica for an hour per week to recreate it as an oil painting.

David and Lana grow more familiar during his visits; he becomes infatuated with her and she enjoys his attentiveness. When David runs out of [[linseed oil]], he convinces Lana to take a trip into town. They buy a book he recommends; the shopkeeper mistakes David for Cliff and offers condolences to David. Later, David dances with Lana to "La Mer", but she rejects his sexual advances. Henry vandalizes David's painting, so David hits him. Lana demands he leave and tries to convince Cliff not to allow him back.

Cliff discovers nude sketches of Lana in David's room on the ship. Cliff punches David, who believes Cliff is unappreciative of what he has. When Cliff confronts Lana, she confesses to her feelings of neglect and to David's advances, which she insists she rejected. The couple reconcile.

Days later, Cliff responds to an alert and takes a spacewalk, but discovers there is no problem. Meanwhile, David uses Cliff's replica to kill Lana and Henry. Cliff discovers his replica is covered in blood and finds the bodies. When Cliff returns to the ship, David wordlessly offers him a seat.

season 6 update: "I don't know what stomach there would be for stories about societies falling apart"|work=[[Radio Times]]|last=Morris|first=Lauren|date=4 May 2020|access-date=10 May [[Netflix]] announced that a sixth ''Black Mirror'' series was in development. Broke and Bones produced the series, while House of Tomorrow's parent company, [[Banijay]], retained ownership.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Ravindran |first1=Manori |title=''Black Mirror'' Returns: New Series in the Works at Netflix (Exclusive) |url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/global/black-mirror-season-6-netflix-1235266891/ |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20230615060651/https://variety.com/2022/tv/global/black-mirror-season-6-netflix-1235266891/ |archive-date=15 June 2023 |date=16 May 2022 |url-status=live |access-date=15 June 2023 }}</ref>

Brooker was the screenwriter for "Beyond the Sea".<ref name="Titles, cast, crew" /> He wrote the episode as a reaction to [[COVID-19 lockdown in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 lockdowns in the UK]],<ref name="THR interview"/> viewing it as a story about [[working from home]].<ref name="NME interview"/> On its initial conception, a character's family are killed by a [[climate change]]-induced [[forest fire]].<ref name="BFI">{{cite AV media|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lw_NY9dOBB4|title=Josh Hartnett and Charlie Brooker on the Black Mirror season six episode Beyond The Sea {{pipe}} BFI Q&A|date=15 June 2023|access-date=7 August 2023|format=Video|publisher=[[British Film Institute]]|via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref>{{rp|1:30}} However, the setting was changed to 1969—inspired by the historical setting of "[[Demon 79]]", the first episode in the sixth series to be written.<ref name="Esquire interview"/> "Beyond the Sea" was influenced by science fiction of the era, and the [[Helter Skelter (scenario)|Helter Skelter]] predictions of the [[Manson Family]] cult active in the 1960s. Brooker wrote the characters to follow behavioural norms of this period,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/06/black-mirror-season-six-charlie-brooker-spoilers|title=''Black Mirror''{{'}}s Charlie Brooker Keeps Finding New Ways to Freak Us Out|work=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]|last=Press|first=Joy|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=7 August 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616162024/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/06/black-mirror-season-six-charlie-brooker-spoilers|url-status=live}}</ref> saying they act differently due to the lack of mobile phones.<ref name="Esquire interview"/>

The episode title "Sea of Tranquility" was considered, in reference to a fictional television show referred to throughout ''Black Mirror''. The final title "Beyond the Sea" references [[Beyond the Sea (song)|an English version]] of "La Mer". Brooker said the song was "haunting" and "timeless".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mashable.com/article/black-mirror-beyond-the-sea-song-meaning|title='Black Mirror's 'Beyond the Sea': What's the significance of the song?|work=[[Mashable]]|last=Haysom|first=Sam|date=23 June 2023|accessdate=7 August 2023|archive-date=7 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230807183957/https://mashable.com/article/black-mirror-beyond-the-sea-song-meaning|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="BFI"/>{{rp|10:00}} Brooker mentioned a number of books in his script that are shown onscreen, including ''[[The Illustrated Man]]'' (1959)—as the [[The Illustrated Man (film)|1969 film]] had scared him—and ''[[Valley of the Dolls (novel)|Valley of the Dolls]]'' (1966), as a joke about Lana living with a replica.<ref name="BFI"/>{{rp|29:30}}

[[File:John Crowley Dinard 2008-10a.jpg|thumb|upright|alt=John Crowley|[[John Crowley (director)|John Crowley]] directed "Beyond the Sea".]]

=== Casting ===
Aaron Paul is among the few actors to have two appearances in ''Black Mirror'', after a voice [[cameo appearance]] in the space-themed series four episode "[[USS Callister|USS ''Callister'']]". He accepted the cameo under the condition that it not preclude him from future appearances, since the series has a nearly-unbroken policy of never using the same screen actor or actress twice in separate episodes. He had also auditioned for a different episode, and was approached for a series five appearance, but could not appear due to other commitments.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.digitalspy.com/tv/black-mirror/news/a869233/black-mirror-aaron-paul-new-role-breaking-bad/ | title = Breaking Bad's Aaron Paul almost landed another role on Black Mirror | first = Sam | last = Warner | date = 25 October 2018 | access-date = 25 October 2018 | work = [[Digital Spy]] | archive-date = 26 October 2018 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20181026064452/http://www.digitalspy.com/tv/black-mirror/news/a869233/black-mirror-aaron-paul-new-role-breaking-bad/ | url-status = live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/black-mirror-director-explains-aaron-paul-kirsten-dunst-uss-callister-cameos-1070949 | title = 'Black Mirror' Director Explains Hidden "USS Callister" Cameos | first = Jackie | last = Strause | date = 2 January 2018 | access-date = 3 January 2018 | website = [[The Hollywood Reporter]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180102202920/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/black-mirror-director-explains-aaron-paul-kirsten-dunst-uss-callister-cameos-1070949 | archive-date = 2018-01-02 | url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Guardian interview"/> Paul was a big ''Black Mirror'' fan and stated that the show had encouraged him to limit his use of technology and social media—to the point of not owning a computer.<ref name="Guardian interview">{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2023/jun/16/aaron-paul-on-black-mirror-ai-and-his-love-of-dark-roles|title='You'd need to talk to my therapist about that': Aaron Paul on Black Mirror, AI and his love of dark roles|work=[[The Guardian]]|last=Jones|first=Daisy|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=17 June 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616230759/https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2023/jun/16/aaron-paul-on-black-mirror-ai-and-his-love-of-dark-roles|url-status=live}}</ref> Paul was friends with Mara prior to filming and had met Hartnett before.<ref name="THR Paul">{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/aaron-paul-black-mirror-episode-beyond-the-sea-breaking-bad-interview-1235530479/|title=Aaron Paul Talks Traumatic 'Black Mirror' Episode, 'Breaking Bad' Reunions and Why He Gravitates to Heavier Roles|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|last=Davids|first=Brian|date=7 July 2023|accessdate=7 August 2023|archive-date=3 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230803063622/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/aaron-paul-black-mirror-episode-beyond-the-sea-breaking-bad-interview-1235530479/|url-status=live}}</ref> He had spent a lot of time on farms and had [[stargazing]] as a hobby since childhood.<ref name="RS interview">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-features/aaron-paul-black-mirror-interview-beyond-the-sea-ai-aliens-1234780023/|title=Aaron Paul Thinks AI Is Scarier Than Any 'Black Mirror' Episode|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|last=Ehrlich|first=Brenna|date=30 June 2023|accessdate=7 August 2023|archive-date=11 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230711144120/https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-features/aaron-paul-black-mirror-interview-beyond-the-sea-ai-aliens-1234780023/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Paul described Cliff as "heavy-handed", but imagined that Cliff saw himself as a "sweet, delicate, nice, loving father" in comparison to his father.<ref name="THR Paul"/> In comparison to Paul, Cliff is "standoffish" and "by the book".<ref name="RS interview"/> He said Cliff had "deep-rooted baggage" and an inability to communicate, but realised this and "started to go down the right path" once learning of David's love for Lana. When filming Cliff's discovery of his family's murder, Paul avoided viewing the set to give realism to his reaction, asking only to know the camera locations.<ref name="THR Paul"/>

Mara was also a [[Fan (person)|fan]] of the series and was keen to work on "Beyond the Sea" because of its exploration of relationships.<ref name="Variety interview"/><ref name="GamesRadar+"/> Mara saw that David, Cliff and Lana all experienced isolation.<ref name="THR interview">{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/black-mirror-beyond-the-sea-ending-josh-hartnett-kate-mara-1235516380/|title=Josh Hartnett, Kate Mara on Their Lockdown-Inspired 'Black Mirror' and Why It's Set in an Alternate 1969|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|last=Strause|first=Jackie|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=17 June 2023|archive-date=17 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230617034532/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/black-mirror-beyond-the-sea-ending-josh-hartnett-kate-mara-1235516380/|url-status=live}}</ref> In Lana's case, she lacks options due to her status as a housewife in the 1960s, but wants her husband to feel present.<ref name="EW interview"/> Hartnett was not present for filming of the scenes where Paul plays David in Cliff's replica.<ref name="Variety interview"/> Instead, rehearsals and discussions focused on this element. According to Hartnett, the key was for Paul to embody David's "internal machinations", not to impersonate him.<ref name="EW interview"/> Mara said it was always clear which character Paul was playing as David is "much more present with Lana" while Cliff is "gone, in so many ways".<ref name="THR interview"/> Paul said he studied Hartnett's manner during rehearsals and wanted to capture his "inherent charm".<ref name="THR Paul"/> Paul and Mara had dance lessons together in preparation for their dance to "La Mer".<ref name="RS interview"/>

Hartnett was offered the role a week before filming began.<ref name="Variety interview">{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/news/black-mirror-salma-hayek-annie-murphy-joan-is-awful-1235645414/|title=Netflix Gave Us Only Four Minutes With the Cast of 'Black Mirror': Read Our Speedy, Spoilery Interviews!|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|last1=Yossman|first1=K. J.|last2=Stephan|first2=Katcy Stephan|last3=Riley|first3=Jenelle|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=7 August 2023|archive-date=3 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230803105335/https://variety.com/2023/tv/news/black-mirror-salma-hayek-annie-murphy-joan-is-awful-1235645414/|url-status=live}}</ref> He said that David is an optimist who represents society's hopefulness towards space exploration.<ref name="EW interview">{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-josh-hartnett-kate-mara-break-down-space-episode/|title=Josh Hartnett and Kate Mara break down their spacefaring Black Mirror episode|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|last=Holub|first=Christian|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=7 August 2023|archive-date=5 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230805091845/https://ew.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-josh-hartnett-kate-mara-break-down-space-episode/|url-status=live}}</ref> Commenting on David's situation, Hartnett said that a person's soul will "atrophy" if "love and connection" are taken from them.<ref name="THR interview"/> Paul believed David's oil painting plan had no initial ulterior motive.<ref name="THR Paul"/> According to Hartnett, David ended up with three choices: to kill himself, Cliff, or Cliff's family. The middle choice would lead to his death indirectly. David decides on the last option as a way to "actually connect" to Cliff, as both of their families will have been murdered.<ref name="EW interview"/>

=== Filming ===
[[File:Skylab labeled.jpg|thumb|upright=1.2|alt=Skylab diagram|[[NASA]]'s first space station, [[Skylab]], was crewed in 1973 and 1974. It was an influence in the design for "Beyond the Sea".]]
After rehearsals in London, three weeks of filming was done in [[Whitstable]], England, in the [[2022 United Kingdom heat waves|summer 2022 heatwaves]].<ref name="THR Paul"/><ref name="NME interview">{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/features/tv-features/black-mirror-netflix-interview-charlie-brooker-cast-episodes-theories-3457066|title='Black Mirror' season six post-watch guide: trivia, set secrets and more|work=[[NME]]|last=Flood|first=Alex|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=16 June 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616174102/https://www.nme.com/features/tv-features/black-mirror-netflix-interview-charlie-brooker-cast-episodes-theories-3457066|url-status=live}}</ref> To represent Cliff's rural American house, the production used a house in Whitstable designed by a homesick American. They let the grass grow to give it an "untouched feeling", added a barn, and redesigned the interior to fit the 1960s.<ref name="Digest">{{cite web|url=https://www.architecturaldigest.com/story/black-mirror-beyond-the-sea-inside-the-making-of-season-6-standout-episode|title=Black Mirror's 'Beyond the Sea': Inside the Making of Season Six's Standout Episode|work=[[Architectural Digest]]|last=Collins|first=Charlotte|date=21 June 2023|accessdate=11 August 2023|archive-date=30 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230630184012/https://www.architecturaldigest.com/story/black-mirror-beyond-the-sea-inside-the-making-of-season-6-standout-episode|url-status=live}}</ref> Filming for David and Lana's shopping trip took place at [[Rye, East Sussex]], England.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/tv/where-was-black-mirror-episode-beyond-the-sea-filmed-3458402|title=Where was 'Black Mirror' episode 'Beyond The Sea' filmed?|work=[[NME]]|last=Starkey|first=Adam|date=21 June 2023|accessdate=11 August 2023|archive-date=28 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230628205207/https://www.nme.com/news/tv/where-was-black-mirror-episode-beyond-the-sea-filmed-3458402|url-status=live}}</ref>

The spaceship's interior was built in [[Twickenham]], London—on the same [[soundstage]] where [[the Beatles]] recorded "[[Get Back]]" (1969).<ref name="Esquire interview">{{cite web|url=https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a44197628/charlie-brooker-black-mirror-interview/|title=''Black Mirror'' Season 6: Charlie Brooker Breaks Down Every Episode|work=[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]|last=Stefansky|first=Emma|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=17 June 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616145405/https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a44197628/charlie-brooker-black-mirror-interview/|url-status=live}}</ref> It was designed with [[NASA]]'s [[Skylab]] in mind, which was launched in 1973. Kramer also took inspiration from the film ''[[2001: A Space Odyssey]]'' (1968), but avoided the "flashing buttons and blinking lights" used in futuristic fiction of the era.<ref name="Digest"/> According to Hartnett, it was designed to be "a little too small", so his height of {{convert|6|ft|3|in|cm}} meant that he struggled to get through doorways.<ref name="GamesRadar+">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/black-mirror-season-6-josh-hartnett-kate-mara-interview/|title=Josh Hartnett and Kate Mara break down Black Mirror's most heartbreaking episode yet|work=[[GamesRadar+]]|last=West|first=Amy|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=7 August 2023|archive-date=28 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230628124344/https://www.gamesradar.com/black-mirror-season-6-josh-hartnett-kate-mara-interview/|url-status=live}}</ref> This brought [[claustrophobia]] to the atmosphere.<ref name="Digest"/>

Three nights of filming took place in [[Valencia]], Spain, where a midcentury home was used for David's residence.<ref name="THR interview"/><ref name="Dezeen">{{cite web|url=https://www.dezeen.com/2023/06/15/black-mirror-production-designer-interview/|title=Black Mirror's latest season a 'mini film festival' says production designer Udo Kramer|work=[[Dezeen]]|last=Carlson|first=Cajsa|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=7 August 2023|archive-date=21 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230721213711/https://www.dezeen.com/2023/06/15/black-mirror-production-designer-interview/|url-status=live}}</ref> According to Kramer, the house was built around a swimming pool and incorporated period details. Walls were added to change its layout and furniture was replaced. Kramer said the design had to be "very serious so that the drama pays off".<ref name="Dezeen"/> Red tiling was replaced by a cream carpet to heighten the "off place" aura of the intruders and the effect of the red hue during the violence.<ref name="Digest"/> Hartnett said the scene where David's family are killed was filmed "at the end of a very long night", time-limited, and emotional for him as a parent.<ref name="THR interview"/>

== Analysis ==
"Beyond the Sea" is a [[science fiction]] and a [[horror fiction|horror]] story.<ref name="Paste"/> It is an example of [[retrofuturism]], showing futuristic technology in a past setting.<ref name="Time"/> According to ''[[Den of Geek]]''{{'}}s Louisa Mellor, its setting is used "as the stage on which to tell a domestic tale".<ref name="DoG"/> Ed Power, writing in ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'', found it reminiscent of the [[Golden Age of Science Fiction]].<ref name="Tele">{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/tv/2023/06/15/black-mirror-season-6-e3-review-beyond-sea/|title=Black Mirror, Beyond the Sea, review: patience is needed – but rewarded – in this meditative sci-fi|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|last=Power|first=Ed|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=17 June 2023|archive-date=17 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230617005435/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/tv/2023/06/15/black-mirror-season-6-e3-review-beyond-sea/|url-status=live}}</ref> Adi Robertson of ''[[The Verge]]'' believed that the 1960s period allowed [[suspension of disbelief]] by the viewer, as its more limited technology creates capacity for its characters' isolation.<ref name="Verge">{{cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2023/6/15/23761949/black-mirror-season-six-beyond-the-sea-aaron-paul-josh-hartnett-review|title=Black Mirror's 'Beyond the Sea' is a slow-motion tragedy in the depths of space|work=[[The Verge]]|last=Robertson|first=Adi|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=11 August 2023|archive-date=1 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230701155710/https://www.theverge.com/2023/6/15/23761949/black-mirror-season-six-beyond-the-sea-aaron-paul-josh-hartnett-review|url-status=live}}</ref> Hartnett noted that the killing of David's replica and his family mirrors the Manson Family's murder of [[Sharon Tate]] in 1969, the same year the episode is set.<ref name="THR interview"/> Kappa, the leader, represents [[Charles Manson]].<ref name="Verge"/>

Before "Beyond the Sea", past settings were featured in ''Black Mirror'' in "[[San Junipero]]" and ''[[Black Mirror: Bandersnatch|Bandersnatch]]''. The former shows pastiches of the 1980s, 1990s and 2000s, while the latter is set in 1984.<ref name="GamesRadar+"/> Its exploration of grief through artificial humans is another commonality with "San Junipero", as well as "[[Be Right Back]]". Robertson said "Be Right Back" is more metaphorical than "Beyond the Sea", using an artificial human as a representation of a character's [[digital footprint]].<ref name="Verge"/> Marital issues, another theme of the episode, were also the subject of "[[The Entire History of You]]".<ref name="Vulture"/>

Robertson characterised the episode as a character study. Cliff and David are initially [[foil (narrative)|foils]], with contrasting uptight and relaxed natures.<ref name="Verge"/> Unlike Cliff, David demonstrates love for his children and wife, as well as interest in art and music. His wealth, job and family makes him "everything American society in 1969 told men they should be", Mellor wrote. Cliff represents an "older style of masculinity", according to Mellor: he is shown chopping wood, [[spearfishing]] and [[Grace (prayer)|saying grace]],<ref name="DoG"/> and he is quite indifferent to his wife and child. According to Ben Rosenstock, in a review for ''[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]'', Lana begins to imagine David as "the Cliff she originally fell in love with", exemplified in her comments about David "wearing her husband like a suit".<ref name="Vulture">{{cite web|url=https://www.vulture.com/article/black-mirror-recap-season-6-episode-3-beyond-the-sea.html|title=''Black Mirror'' Recap: Rocket Men|last=Rosenstock|first=Ben|work=[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=11 August 2023|archive-date=28 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230628235933/https://www.vulture.com/article/black-mirror-recap-season-6-episode-3-beyond-the-sea.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

{{multiple image
| align       = right
| total_width = 250
| image1      = Aaron Paul SDDC 2019.jpg
| alt1        = Aaron Paul
| image2      = Josh Hartnett SDCC 2014.jpg
| alt2        = Josh Hartnett
| footer      = [[Aaron Paul]] ''(left)'' and [[Josh Hartnett]] ''(right)'' portrayed Cliff and David, respectively. The episode explores each character's masculinity.}}
In ''[[i (newspaper)|i]]'', Emily Baker wrote that the episode exemplified how "men use violence against women as a tool".<ref name="i">{{cite web|url=https://inews.co.uk/culture/television/black-mirror-beyond-the-sea-netflix-review-josh-hartnett-aaron-paul-2412348|title=Black Mirror: Beyond the Sea, Netflix, review: Josh Hartnett and Aaron Paul's episode is one of the best yet|work=[[i (newspaper)|i]]|last=Baker|first=Emily|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=11 August 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616081530/https://inews.co.uk/culture/television/black-mirror-beyond-the-sea-netflix-review-josh-hartnett-aaron-paul-2412348|url-status=live}}</ref> An example from Mellor is that David kills Lana as revenge against Cliff. Mellor commented that the men "treat wives and children as the property of husbands", in line with 1960s norms, and that "nothing is so dangerous to women and children as a man with a bruised ego".<ref name="DoG">{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-beyond-the-sea-review/|title=Black Mirror Season 6 Episode 3 Review: Beyond the Sea|work=[[Den of Geek]]|last=Mellor|first=Louisa|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=11 August 2023|archive-date=28 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230628123805/https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-beyond-the-sea-review/|url-status=live}}</ref> Cliff is terse towards his wife and hits his son to control his behaviour.<ref name="i"/> Bryanna Arens, also writing in ''Den of Geek'', believed that both Cliff and David show [[toxic masculinity]], with a "rigid and limiting" understanding of manhood. They do not discuss their emotions, and Cliff is surprised when he learns that David cried in grief.<ref name="DoG Ending">{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-why-beyond-the-seas-divisive-ending-works/|title=Black Mirror: Why Beyond the Sea's Divisive Ending Works|work=[[Den of Geek]]|last=Arens|first=Brynna|date=20 June 2023|accessdate=11 August 2023|archive-date=29 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230629121214/https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-why-beyond-the-seas-divisive-ending-works/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Robertson found the narrative "strikingly generous" towards both men: for instance, Cliff's decision to move to an isolated location makes sense given the violence against David's family<ref name="Verge"/> (although the murder of David's family and his replica occurs after Cliff has already moved). However, Mellor believed that Cliff makes decisions to limit Lana's socialisation, such as rejecting her garden party idea to keep her "from the temptations and threats of other people".<ref name="DoG"/> Arens analysed that David believes he is owed what he wants: he draws Lana naked without consent and continues caressing her after she tells him to stop.<ref name="DoG Ending"/>

Lana's books hint at the episode's plot. She is first seen reading ''[[Airport (Hailey novel)|Airport]]'' (1968), in which the protagonist's intense job leads to marital issues. ''[[Valley of the Dolls (novel)|Valley of the Dolls]]'', which portrays sex and female friendship in [[New York City]], may remind Lana of her previous lifestyle. Its characters suffer issues with relationships and loneliness. In ''[[The Moon Is a Harsh Mistress]]'' (1966), the book David recommends to Lana, a [[lunar colony]] revolts to free itself from Earth's control; its society has two men per woman.<ref name="Mashable">{{cite web|url=https://mashable.com/article/black-mirror-beyond-the-sea-season-6-clues-books|title='Black Mirror' dropped tons of bookish clues in 'Beyond the Sea'|work=[[Mashable]]|last=Connellan|first=Shannon|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=11 August 2023|archive-date=5 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230805221248/https://mashable.com/article/black-mirror-beyond-the-sea-season-6-clues-books|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Reception ==
On the review aggregator [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the episode holds an approval rating of 87% based on 15 reviews.<ref>{{cite Rotten Tomatoes |type=tv |id=black_mirror |season=6 |episode=3 |access-date=11 August 2023}}</ref> It received five stars from ''i'';<ref name="i"/> ''[[The Independent]]'', ''The Daily Telegraph'' and ''Den of Geek'' rated it four stars out of five;<ref name="Indy"/><ref name="Tele"/><ref name="DoG"/> ''Vulture'' gave it two stars.<ref name="Vulture"/> Several critics saw it as the best episode in the sixth series.<ref name="Vanity review"/><ref name="Paste"/><ref name="i"/>

Critics identified the episode's tone as an asset. ''The Independent''{{'}}s Nick Hilton and ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]''{{'}}s Judy Berman praised its tone as similar to the programme's best installments, describing it as a "gloomy, high-concept" episode and one with a "poetic, emotional register", respectively.<ref name="Indy">{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-episodes-ranked-b2357292.html|title=Black Mirror season six review: Charlie Brooker's sci-fi mishmash needs to stop messing with a winning formula|work=[[The Independent]]|last=Hilton|first=Nick|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=16 June 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616020939/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-episodes-ranked-b2357292.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Time">{{cite magazine|url=https://time.com/6287513/black-mirror-season-6-review/|title=What Even Is ''Black Mirror'' Anymore?|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|last=Berman|first=Judy|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=11 August 2023|archive-date=15 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715005440/https://time.com/6287513/black-mirror-season-6-review/|url-status=live}}</ref> Robertson found that it was "driven by empathy", a rarity in the series.<ref name="Verge"/> ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]''{{'}}s Leila Jordan lauded it as "enthralling and horrifying in all the best ways",<ref name="Paste">{{cite web|url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/tv/netflix/black-mirror-season-6-review|title=''Black Mirror'' Struggles to Imagine the Future in an Uneven Season 6|work=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]|last=Jordan|first=Leila|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=11 August 2023|archive-date=24 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724170744/https://www.pastemagazine.com/tv/netflix/black-mirror-season-6-review|url-status=live}}</ref> while Power reviewed it as "unusually contemplative" and "lacking in Brooker's familiar vicious wit" under the direction of Crowley, a "master of mood".<ref name="Tele"/> Less positively, ''[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]''{{'}}s Richard Lawson said that it had "solemn weight" but lacked the "zeitgeist verve" of other installments.<ref name="Vanity review">{{cite web|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/06/black-mirror-season-6-review|title=''Black Mirror''{{'}}s Odd Future Feels Stuck in the Past|work=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]|last=Lawson|first=Richard|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=11 August 2023|archive-date=20 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230620063648/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/06/black-mirror-season-6-review|url-status=live}}</ref> Daniel D'Addario criticised it in ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' as resembling "an attempt to provide dramatic bona fides by going as grim as possible".<ref name="Variety">{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-1235644259/|title='Black Mirror' Season 6 Is a Refreshingly Uncynical Return to Form: TV Review|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|last=D'Addario|first=Daniel|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=11 August 2023|archive-date=25 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230625033800/https://variety.com/2023/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-1235644259/|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Kate Mara by Gage Skidmore.jpg|thumb|upright|alt=Kate Mara|[[Kate Mara]]'s performance as Lana garnered praise from reviewers.]]
The cast garnered acclaim, with reviewers identifying the episode as character-driven.<ref name="Verge"/><ref name="Indy"/> For ''[[The A.V. Club]]'', Kayleigh Dray wrote: "The power in this piece comes from its powerhouse performances"—namely, Culkin's "menacing turn", Mara's "gentle warmth", and the "ever-growing intensity of Paul and Hartnett".<ref name="AVClub">{{cite web|url=https://www.avclub.com/black-mirror-season-6-tv-review-netflix-charlie-brooker-1850540964|title=''Black Mirror'' season 6 review: Through the past, darkly|website=[[The A.V. Club]]|last=Dray|first=Kayleigh|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=11 August 2023|archive-date=20 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720184040/https://www.avclub.com/black-mirror-season-6-tv-review-netflix-charlie-brooker-1850540964|url-status=live}}</ref> Lawson praised the "sharp, layered performances";<ref name="Vanity review"/> D'Addario found the cast, particularly Mara, capable of "acting out big emotions with delicate restraint".<ref name="Variety"/> Neil Armstrong of ''[[BBC Culture]]'' believed that Paul gave the best performance in the series, despite the difficulty of showing emotion beneath his character's restraint.<ref name="BBC">{{cite web |last=Armstrong |first=Neil |title=Black Mirror season six review: Charlie Brooker's series is 'a show that revels in its twists' |url=https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20230614-black-mirror-season-six-review-charlie-brookers-series-is-a-show-that-revels-in-its-twists |website=[[BBC Culture]] |date=15 June 2023 |accessdate=11 August 2023 |archive-date=20 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720174319/https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20230614-black-mirror-season-six-review-charlie-brookers-series-is-a-show-that-revels-in-its-twists |url-status=live }}</ref> Baker also praised the "heartbreakingly raw turn" of Paul, and of Hartnett's transition from sympathetic to villainous. Baker reviewed Mara as the "emotional pivot" of the drama and said she gave "the performance of her career".<ref name="i"/> In a negative review, Ehrlich nonetheless praised the cast.<ref name="RS"/> Rosenstock, contrastingly, believed the acting was too mute; he criticised Paul's distinction between Cliff and David as too subtle, Lana's lack of liveliness around David, and the lack of explanation for Cliff's stiff manner.<ref name="Vulture"/>

Reception to the plot was more polarised. For instance, whilst Dray believed the technology was "a poorly disguised plot device" and ''Far Out''{{'}}s Calum Russell found the [[worldbuilding]] lacking, Hilton thought the episode "tackles big sci-fi issues{{nbsp}}... with superb confidence".<ref name="AVClub"/><ref name="FarOut">{{cite web|url=https://faroutmagazine.co.uk/beyond-the-sea-could-have-been-the-best-black-mirror-episode/|title='Beyond the Sea' could have been the best 'Black Mirror' episode|work=Far Out|last=Russell|first=Calum|date=1 July 2023|accessdate=11 August 2023|archive-date=11 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230811215148/https://faroutmagazine.co.uk/beyond-the-sea-could-have-been-the-best-black-mirror-episode/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Indy"/> Hilton compared it favourably to the space-themed science fiction films ''[[Moon (2009 film)|Moon]]'' (2009) and ''[[Sunshine (2007 film)|Sunshine]]'' (2007).<ref name="Indy"/> Rosenstock found the plot easy to anticipate,<ref name="Vulture"/> while Lawson wrote that "Brooker smartly pushes past" the obvious early twists "toward a far bleaker place".<ref name="Vanity review"/> Russell critiqued that the premise brought a "flood of possibilities" but the writers "frustratingly decided to go down the least enticing path". The episode would have been better, Russell suggested, if Lana fell in love with David rather than the reverse.<ref name="FarOut"/> The ending was praised as "stunning" and "admirably twisted" by Baker and Rosenstock, respectively.<ref name="i"/><ref name="Vulture"/>

Critics also dissented on the episode's length. Jordan saw it as a "well-told, concise story".<ref name="Paste"/> Hilton suggested the climax was rushed and another 30 minutes could have developed the piece.<ref name="Indy"/> Contrastingly, according to Power, some viewers may find it too slow in comparison to more "anarchic" episodes.<ref name="Tele"/> Rosenstock said the "pregnant pauses" do not add value and [[Alan Sepinwall]] of ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' found that every [[unit of action|beat]] is elongated and it "takes forever to set its plot in motion".<ref name="Vulture"/><ref name="RS">{{cite web|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-mocks-netflix-annie-murphy-salma-hayek-1234770401/|title='Black Mirror' Season Six Takes Aim at Netflix But Feels Stuck in the Past|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|last=Sepinwall|first=Alan|author-link=Alan Sepinwall|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=11 August 2023|archive-date=30 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230630161000/https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-mocks-netflix-annie-murphy-salma-hayek-1234770401/|url-status=live}}</ref>
